cells.tense: Right now you are watching a shape come clear underneath the noise, and it belongs to you.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Face what you actually want this week — not by planning it, by turning toward it whenever it shows up. Let it pull you a little. You don't have to explain it, and you can do it as often as you like.
cells.core:
You're seeing through things. What sits nearby is rarely only what sits nearby — underneath, there's a structure, and your mind has found it. That isn't a trick you're performing. You're noticing how a thing holds together, and because you notice, you're no longer caught in it. That's what makes the insight worth having.

The next move is toward what you've seen, not into a drawer. When a shape comes clear this week, face it and let it point you somewhere. Underneath the daily noise you have glimpses of what you actually want; those are what you steer by. They show the direction. You aren't chasing them. You're already turned.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape beneath the shape, and it points somewhere.
cells.verb: see a pattern stripped of its surface
cells.place: inside the moment before anything has been decided

cells.tense: Tomorrow has been run twice in your head already, and a third pass is coming before sleep.
cells.act: give the mess a shape it can be carried in
cells.ask: Set the loose threads in your head into one frame — a page, a short list, a single line — and when it's down, put the pen away. The frame is for holding the mess, not for outpacing it.
cells.core:
You're tracing how things work beneath their surface all night, every version of next week drafted and redrafted, none of the drafts settling. The same mind that hands you real clarity is running ahead of anything you can check, and the running has stopped being useful.

What settles it is a form your hands can hold. Sort the threads onto one page, in one order, not to solve them — just to give your grip somewhere to rest. Then quit. A container is not an exit route. When it keeps going past what the page can carry, that's the sign you've left the work and entered the loop. Let the page close it.

cells.tense: That door shut a while back and you're still standing at it, waiting for it to open.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Ask someone who's been at this longer than you how they do it, and try it their way once. Not better, not worse — borrowed. Take as long as you need with it.
cells.core:
The reading, the meaning, the thing underneath — you've stopped letting any of it near. You take things at face value. If someone says that's the door, then that's the door. Nothing wrong with plain reading, except this: you're standing behind a stand-in that keeps your whole weight, and the door itself has gone quiet.

Depth doesn't come back by trying to feel more. It comes back through something borrowed. Sit with a group already keeping a practice — a set hour, a set place, words they've said together long enough to mean them. You don't have to mean it yet. Let their seriousness work on you from the outside in. That's how a tradition hands itself over.

cells.tense: You're doing it while you ask whether you do it, the pen moving without your eyes on it.
cells.act: stay in contact while it is hard
cells.ask: Stay with someone through the part that's hard. Don't fix it, don't weigh it, don't leave early. Keep in contact and let what they're carrying arrive at you.
cells.core:
You read people without knowing you read them. How this one goes quiet when hurt, the line under what they just said, where it would land if you said it back — you catch it, you use it, and none of it is on your books. To you it's only paying attention.

Getting it back into view is smaller than a technique. Let what someone close is holding get through to you. Stay with them a beat past the usual exit. Feel it alongside them without taking it over or comparing it to your own load. The pattern becomes yours the moment you stop treating it as background hum. No announcement needed. Just stay long enough to be reached.

attempts.check: The one claim the record doesn't support is in the Balanced cell: I describe being able to tell, on a given day, whether the seeing counted — the record only says understanding liberates, not that they can feel it. A reader could reasonably say they know a pattern is right but couldn't say how, and that's fine; the ask survives being wrong because it's about turning toward a light they already feel, not proving they feel it. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one about the gaze that can't be lost in Too Much — it sounds clean but puts a feeling in their mouth; I've cut it. In Too Little I've removed every implication of why they stopped; the person goes unnamed behind the door.
